root_idea.summary: The supplied evidence centers on forceful severity: قَمْطَرِير describes a distressful or calamitous condition, especially one that makes the brow knit.
root_idea.development: The evidence records a severity branch alongside a separately attested nominal branch for a repository of writings and a Form IV verb meaning to become distressful. No Maqāyīs entry is supplied to establish a fuller historical root development.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The Quran-attested adjective is presented under its normalized dictionary citation form.

senses.definition: Distressful, calamitous, intensely severe; of a day, one that makes the brow knit.
senses.usage_conditions: Quran-attested in the expression describing a distressful or calamitous day. The brow-knitting wording explains the effect or character of the severity rather than imposing a restriction on the kind of thing described.

other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Classical Form IV verb; the supplied lexical example has a day as its subject.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A repository for books or writings, made of woven reeds and resembling a safat.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A nominal lexical branch, with the recorded plural قَمَاطِرُ.
Attested in the Classical collocation شَرٌّ قَمْطَرِيرٌ; this broader collocational use is kept separate from the Quranic description of a distressful day.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Form IV verb meaning is represented under its derived verb headword.
Repository-for-books meaning is represented as a separate nominal branch.
Distressful or calamitous day, including the brow-knitting explanation, is Quran-attested.
The collocation for intense evil is represented as a broader Classical use.

cautions: The Quranic occurrence is the inflected form قَمْطَرِيرًا; the public headword is normalized to the adjective citation form قَمْطَرِير.
